what_this_is: the end-to-end fixture: a ten-thousand-pair library carrying all three of the report's output classes, with toy indexes built from its own sequence. It is a test of whether every report section is filled, and it is NOT a benchmark: no number from it belongs in results/.

ms2.role: known virus, in the toy nucleotide index, must be subtracted as tier 1
ms2.why: Enterobacteria phage MS2, 3,569 nt, four non-overlapping ORFs whose roles are maturation, coat, lysis and replicase. The repo's gene-level asymmetry work is stated in exactly those roles (SPEC 2.2), so a fixture carrying them exercises the per-gene ranking rather than only a whole-contig identity.

pmmov.role: divergent-but-related virus: mutated here, the real one in the toy protein index only
pmmov.why: Pepper mild mottle virus, 6,357 nt. A plant virus that is one of the most abundant RNA viruses in human wastewater, so a wastewater fixture carrying it is not an arbitrary choice.

ecoli.role: bacterial background, in the toy classifier library and the toy SILVA
ecoli.why: E. coli K-12 MG1655. A 16 kb slice spanning the rrnB operon, so the fixture has ribosomal sequence in it: rRNA is about a third of the discriminating library and the stage that anchors against SILVA has nothing to do without any.

error_rate.basis: measured reference-free from self-overlapping pairs of SRR23973193 (results/berlin_quality/, CLAUDE.md)

divergent_arm.rejection_rule: a substitution that would make a stop codon inside any annotated CDS, or touch a start codon, is rejected
divergent_arm.basis: measured on this build, not stated: the mapping from a nucleotide rate to a protein identity runs through the genetic code and the rejection rule.
